Explore Life Insurance Plans in India by Need

Term Plans

Pure protection for a chosen period. It is designed to provide a death benefit to the nominee if the life assured dies while the policy is in force.

ULIP Plans

Plans that combine life cover with market-linked investment funds. Returns depend on market performance, fund choice, charges and policy conditions.

Savings Plans

Plans that combine life cover with structured savings and defined policy benefits. Guarantees, if any, apply only as stated in the policy.

Child Plans

Goal-oriented plans designed to support milestones such as higher education and marriage while protecting the plan if the parent dies.

Retirement and Pension Plans

Solutions that can help build a retirement corpus or convert funds into regular income through pension or annuity options.

Health Plans

Protection solutions for eligible employees, borrowers or members under a master policy.

Group Insurance Plans

Employer, lender and member-group solutions that provide protection to eligible individuals under a master policy.

What Is Life Insurance?

Life insurance is a contract between a policyholder and an insurer. In return for the premiums paid, the insurer provides certain pre-decided benefits when a covered event occurs, subject to the policy terms. 


The core purpose of life insurance is to deal with uncertainty of life. A classic life insurance policy ensures the nominee receives the death benefit if the life assured (i.e., the policyholder) passes away while an eligible policy is in force. However, there are other life insurance plans that also offer savings, market-linked growth, guaranteed benefits or retirement income depending on the product selected.

Why Is Life Insurance Important?

Income often supports much more than monthly bills. It may fund a family’s lifestyle, loan repayments, children’s goals, care for parents and long-term savings. Life insurance helps create a financial fallback when that income stops unexpectedly.

Explore Plans
Replace Lost Income

A death benefit can help dependents manage regular household expenses and maintain financial continuity after the loss of an earning member.

Protect Assets from Outstanding Debt

Adequate cover can help a family repay home loans, personal loans and other liabilities without being forced to sell assets earmarked for future goals.

Keep Major Goals Moving

The right policy can help protect plans for education, marriage, retirement or legacy creation when life does not unfold as expected.

Key Benefits of Life Insurance Plans

Financial Protection

Life cover can provide a financial cushion to nominees when the life assured dies during the policy term, subject to the contract.

Goal-Based Saving

Savings-oriented plans can encourage disciplined long-term contributions and offer policy benefits aligned with future milestones.

Growth or Income Options

Depending on the product, policyholders may choose market-linked growth, guaranteed benefits, regular income or annuity options. Market-linked returns are not guaranteed.

Potential Tax Benefits

Eligible premiums and policy proceeds may receive tax treatment under prevailing law, subject to product conditions, policy dates and the taxpayer’s circumstances.

How to Choose the Right Life Insurance Policy?

Explore Plans

Decide whether your first priority is family protection, savings, wealth creation, a child’s goal or retirement income.

Assess your family's monthly expenses, outstanding loans and future goals to arrive at a suitable sum assured and premium budget.

Compare term, endowment, ULIP and savings plans based on your protection needs, investment horizon and risk appetite.

Choose a premium you can continue paying across the full premium payment term. A large policy that lapses may fail when protection is needed.

Review the benefit illustration, exclusions, surrender rules, charges, riders, claim process and policy wording. Disclose health, occupation, income and lifestyle details truthfully.

Who Can Purchase a Life Insurance Policy?

Adults who meet a plan’s entry-age, income, health, residency, documentation and underwriting requirements may apply for life insurance. A policyholder may buy cover on their own life or, where permitted, propose a policy for another person with an insurable interest. Acceptance, premium and cover are decided after underwriting. 

18-25 Yrs

Start personal protection early, cover education debt and begin long-term goal planning.

26-35 Yrs

Protect a spouse, parents or young family; cover a home loan; build savings for future milestones.

36-45 Yrs

Review a growing protection gap, children’s goals, business obligations and retirement savings. 

46-55 Yrs

Reassess liabilities, dependents, legacy needs and the transition from accumulation to retirement planning. 

56+ Yrs

Consider retirement income, estate needs and plan options available within product-specific entry-age rules. 

*This is a life-stage guide, not an eligibility table. Entry-age, maturity age, medical requirements and available benefits vary by product.

Smart Life Insurance Plans Built for Changing Milestones

First Job

Start with affordable protection, cover personal liabilities and begin disciplined long-term planning.

Marriage or Partnership

Review income replacement needs and choose a nominee so the household has financial continuity.

Home Loan

Increase cover so a surviving family is not forced to fund EMIs or sell the home after a loss of income.

Parenthood

Protect day-to-day needs and future education goals; review whether existing cover is still enough.

Peak Earning or Business Years

Reassess larger liabilities, business responsibilities, wealth goals and retirement contributions.

Approaching Retirement

Reduce protection gaps that no longer exist, evaluate legacy needs and plan a dependable retirement-income strategy

When Should You Buy A Life Insurance Policy?

You should ideally buy a life insurance policy when one or more people depends on your income. Additionally, having a life insurance policy also helps when you either have a long-term debt or a future family goal that would be at risk if you were no longer there to fund it.

Explore Plans
When you have your first regular income

Life protection is more affordable early in life, subject to health, underwriting and plan terms. 

When you get married or have children

Adding enough cover to replace household income and protect shared plans makes sense. 

When you have major liabilities

Review whether the life cover amount could clear the liability without consuming other family assets. 

When planning for child education

Include education, childcare and the number of years the family may require support. 

When your income increases

With higher income comes lifestyle upgrade. Hence, getting a life insurance policy helps cover the protection gap.
